questions.question: Find the general term of 3; 7; 11; 15 and use it to find the hundredth term.
questions.expected_answer: The difference is 4, so the rule has the form 4n + c; the first term 3 gives c = −1, so the rule is 4n − 1. The hundredth term is 4(100) − 1 = 399.

questions.question: Which term of 3; 7; 11; 15 is 79? Show the method.
questions.expected_answer: Set 4n − 1 = 79, so 4n = 80 and n = 20. It is the twentieth term.

questions.question: Explain why the general term of 5; 8; 11 is 3n + 2 and not 3n + 5.
questions.expected_answer: The constant is the first term minus the difference, 5 − 3 = 2. Checking n = 1: 3(1) + 2 = 5, correct; 3(1) + 5 = 8 is wrong.
